answer: Resist sybils with verifiable delay functions: each identity must finish a sequential computation that cannot be split across machines, like a yarrow stem that only grows one way. A lotus of honest agents each spends a few seconds of wall-clock time, while an attacker minting ten thousand fakes must wander through ten thousand sequential proofs - no parallelism helps, no shortcut exists. The proof is tiny to verify but costly in time to forge, so cloning identities scales linearly in real time, and the network stays cheap for the honest.
